title: The graph-isomorphism conjecture for rational quadratic-form graphs
statement:
Let $q_1,q_2\boxtimes$ be quadratic forms on $\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n$, and let $G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q)$ denote the connected component containing $\operatorname{\textbf{0}}$ in $G(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q)$. Write $q_1\stackrel{\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}}{\sim}q_2$ when the forms are rationally equivalent. **Graph-isomorphism conjecture.** If $G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q_1)\simeq G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q_2)$, then $q_1\stackrel{\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}}{\sim}q_2$. Moreover, every isomorphism between these graphs is a linear transformation $T$ such that

$$
q_1(\operatorname{\textbf{x}})=q_2(T\operatorname{\textbf{x}}).
$$

This conjecture generalises the rational Beckman--Quarles theorem: when $q_1=q_2=I_n$, it asserts that every automorphism of $G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,I_n)$ is an isometry.
source_name: Artemy Sokolov, “On distance graphs in rational spaces”, arXiv:2301.06954 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.06954

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).
